name: Search field
summary: Lets people type what they are looking for.
description: A search field collects a search term: a query for a whole site, a filter for a list. It is a Text field with a search glyph at its start, exposed to assistive technology as a search box, and whose clear control the platform provides. It has a visible label, which may be the only word next to it (Search), and an optional description; it has no error state: a search that finds nothing is reported by the results, not by the field.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the error message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.
Box holding the control and the search glyph drawn over its start edge.
The editable box: the native search input, drawn by the component with the search glyph over its start edge. Receives focus, holds the term and shows the placeholder while empty.
Search glyph of the icon font at the start of the control, saying what the field is for. Hidden from assistive technology, which learns it from the role.
Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, value text and inline padding take the height, the text size and the inline padding of the Button of the same size; the label takes the text size of the value; the description takes the helper sizes.

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (28 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (44 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Short hint shown while the field is empty (what can be searched: Search projects). Never the label.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Focus on the control, from the keyboard or a pointer: an editable field shows the shared focus ring outside its border however it was focused.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and error message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.
Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius and the border width do not change.
The search glyph sits over the start edge of the control, which reserves room for it with padding-inline-start.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description is exposed as the accessible description; the placeholder is exposed as a placeholder, not as the name.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.
In browsers that provide a clear control, clears the term.

guidelines.text: Expose the searchbox role, the name, the value and the disabled state through the platform's native search control, so assistive technology announces it as a search field.

Use the native input type=search without a list attribute: it exposes the searchbox role and may take the platform's look and clear control. The clear control is the browser's: the component neither styles nor removes it.
Every search field has a visible label associated with the control programmatically, even when it is just Search; the glyph alone is not a label.
Associate the label with a label element whose for attribute names the control's id, and the description with aria-describedby.
The placeholder is a short hint of what can be searched, never the label: it disappears as soon as people type, and is not exposed as the name when a label exists.
The search glyph is decorative and hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true": an icon-font glyph is written as its ligature name, which would otherwise be read with the value.

Label, value and description contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.03:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.78:1 and 8.86:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.40:1. The glyph is decoration and needs no contrast of its own (6.08:1 and 6.40:1 anyway). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 12.78:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest, 12.09:1 and 10.33:1 on the hover tint; the focus ring 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. Disabled is exempt.
A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus, drawn outside its border.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, which browsers match whenever an editable field has focus, pointer or keyboard.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 28, 36 and 44 pixels.

The label and description are set from 12 to 16 px, under the large text size of the contrast criterion (18 pt, about 24 px), so their colors keep 4.5:1. WCAG sets no minimum text size: it asks that text resize up to 200 % without loss of content or functionality, which the box allows because its height is a minimum that grows with larger text.
A disabled field leaves the focus order.

A search field is an editable text field that displays a search icon, a clear button and placeholder text; use placeholder text to help people know what they can search for. The small and medium sizes (28 and 36 pt) fall under the 44 x 44 pt hit region on iOS today; the large size (44 pt) reaches it.
Apple's recommended minimum text size is 11 pt on iOS and iPadOS; the 12 pt text of the description is above it.
Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; all three sizes (28, 36 and 44 dp) fall under it on Android today.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The label says what is searched: Search, Search projects, Filter by name. Sentence case, no colon.
The placeholder gives an example of a query or the scope (Name, email or role), never the label.
A search field has no error message: an empty result is reported next to the results, with what to try next.

examples.name: Medium, with a value and description

decisions.text: The label of the Search field takes the text size of the value, and the description the helper sizes, as the Text field's (decision label-help-text-sizes of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): label small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px; description small 12 px, medium 12 px, large 14 px. Each is a typography token per size. pnpm validate compares search-field.label.typography.*, search-field.description.typography.* with the Text field's. Changes the single 14 px style that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state; everything else they state is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep the single 14 px style for the label, the description and the message; B, the label follows the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text stays 14 px; C, the label follows the field and the help text takes Figma's helper sizes (12 / 12 / 14 px), chosen; D, Figma's sizes (label 12 / 14 / 16 px, help text 12 / 12 / 14 px, compact line height), rejected because the label would be smaller than the value at the small size and the Typography foundation would need an exception. A label above a field reads at the field's own size, and the help text is secondary to what it describes.

decisions.text: The inline padding of the box of the Search field is the inline padding of the Button without an icon, as the Text field's (decision padding-inline-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 8 px, medium 12 px, large 16 px, at the end of the text. The start padding that clears the glyph (28, 36 and 40 px) is the Search field's own and sums the glyph's margin, size and gap. The decision keeps the values the box already had: no token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the inline padding of the Button without an icon (8 / 12 / 16 px), chosen; B, Figma's 6 / 8 / 10 px; C, the Button's label-side padding (8 / 8 / 10 px), rejected here because it belongs to the question of a leading icon in the field. A field and a Button of the same size start their text at the same inset.

decisions.text: The minimum height of the box of the Search field takes the height of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision box-height-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 28 px, medium 36 px, large 44 px, so a search field and the button next to it line up. pnpm validate compares search-field.control.min-height.* with the Text field's. The search glyph (16, 20, 24 px) stays centred in the height, and the start padding that clears it is unchanged. Changes the 32 / 40 / 48 px minimum heights that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state; everything else they state is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep 32 / 40 / 48 px (one step taller than the Button of the same size); B, the Button's heights 28 / 36 / 44 px, chosen; C, the height Figma's padding gives with the new text (33.6 / 40 / 44 px), which matches neither the Button nor today's; D, Figma's heights rounded up (36 / 40 / 44 px). A field and a Button of the same size line up (a search field next to its button, a form row), and the large size reaches the 44 pt that Apple recommends. The hit region of the small and medium sizes is a later step, as for the Button.

decisions.text: The value and placeholder text of the Search field takes the text size of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision value-text-button-size of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px, regular weight, normal letter spacing and the tight line height (1.2). pnpm validate compares search-field.control.typography.* with the Text field's. The search glyph's size is its own tokens (16, 20, 24 px), so the 28 / 36 / 40 px start padding that clears it is unchanged. Supersedes sizes: the heights, inline padding, border, corners and the 14 px label and description of that decision are unchanged here; only the text of the large size (20 to 16 px) and the line height (1.5 to 1.2) change.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep today's text (small 14, medium 16, large 20 px, line height 1.5: the large size breaks the rule); B, the Button's whole label style (medium weight, compact line height 1.0, tight letter spacing), rejected because people's content would look like a control label, descenders and accents would touch the line, and the Typography foundation would need an exception; C, the Button's text size with the Typography foundation's single-line style (regular weight, normal letter spacing, tight line height 1.2), chosen; D, the Button's text size with the line height 1.5, rejected because that line height is meant for running text.

decisions.text: The Search field always renders the same box as the Text field of the same size and state: height, inline padding, text, border, corners, colors, focus ring, label, description and motion are the Text field's (it has no severity, message or read-only state: decision no-error-state). A Text field decision on any of these applies to the Search field in the same change: pnpm validate fails when a Search field token differs from the Text field token at the same place (MIRRORS in scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs, decision field-family-mirrors of the Text field). The glyph and the start padding that clears it are its own: the start padding (control.padding-inline-start.*) is a sum, glyph margin + glyph size + the gap before the text (28, 36, 40 px today), so a step that changes the box's inline padding, the glyph size or the glyph margin recomputes it. The mirror covers rendering only: a contract decision is asked for the Search field too.
decisions.rationale: Nothing tied the three plain fields to the Text field: a decision on its box left them behind. Mirroring them lets every rendering step of the Text field refinement change the four in the same commit, and pnpm validate prove they agree, where the alternatives (the Text field alone, with a closing step per sibling or an issue for the others) leave the siblings out of step in between. The Select is not mirrored now: it gets its own step later, with the complex controls.

decisions.text: The control follows the Text field's colors: a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the glyph the tertiary icon color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A search glyph (the icon font) sits over the start edge of the control at 16, 20 or 24 px by size, 8 px from the edge; the control reserves 28, 36 or 40 px of start padding for it. It is hidden from assistive technology; the role says what the field is for.
A search field has no invalid or read-only state and no error message: an empty result is reported by the results. The clear control is the browser's.

changelog.note: Decision label-help-text-sizes (Text field decision of the same name): the label scales with the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text shrinks (12 / 12 / 14 px) (search-field.label.typography: one 14 px style becomes small, medium and large, font size body.size.sm to sm / md / md, line height normal 1.5 to tight 1.2; search-field.description.typography: body.size.sm to xs / xs / sm, so 14 px becomes 12 / 12 / 14 px; weights, normal line height and letter spacing kept). The Size property now affects the label, the description. pnpm validate now fails when the label and the value alias different font size tokens. Colors unchanged; contrast re-measured on levels 0 to 3: description 12.78:1 (levels 0 and 2) and 12.09:1 (levels 1 and 3) in light mode, 8.86:1, 8.11:1, 7.43:1 and 6.65:1 on levels 0 to 3 in dark mode, the same on every platform; 4.5:1 required (WCAG 1.4.3), the lowest being 6.65:1.

Decision padding-inline-button (Text field decision of the same name): the inline padding (search-field.control.padding-inline.*) is the Button's inline padding without an icon at the same size. Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision box-height-button (Text field decision of the same name): the minimum height takes the height of the Button of the same size (search-field.control.min-height.*: 32 / 40 / 48 px become 28 / 36 / 44 px). The glyph and the start padding that clears it are unchanged. Target size (WCAG 2.5.8): every size stays above 24 x 24 CSS px. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Decision value-text-button-size (Text field decision of the same name): the value and placeholder text takes the text size of the Button of the same size (small 14, medium 16, large 16 px; the large size was 20 px), with the tight line height (search-field.control.typography.*: large font size body.size.lg to body.size.md, line height normal to tight). The glyph does not depend on the text size: the start padding sums are unchanged. Supersedes sizes. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Decision same-box-as-text-field (Text field decision field-family-mirrors): the Search field is a mirror of the Text field, so every Text field decision on the box applies here in the same change and pnpm validate compares the tokens; its glyph tokens and start padding are declared as its own, and the start padding is a sum to recompute with the box. No token, CSS or template change: the tokens already resolve to the Text field's values in every platform and mode, so sizes, colors and contrast are unchanged.

Follows the Iconography foundation 0.3.0 (decision optical-size-24): the icon glyph is drawn for optical size 24 instead of 20 (search-field.icon.optical-size → font.icon.optical-size.24). Sizes and colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 7 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel). Dark: 10 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); control.border-color.default reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 5.79 → 5.77:1, 6.36 → 6.40:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.14 → 12.09:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.

Initial draft (decisions field-colors, sizes, search-glyph, no-error-state). Native search input in a wrapper with a label element, a search glyph and a description; states default, hover, focus-visible, disabled; sizes small, medium, large. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label and value 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, placeholder and glyph 6.08 / 6.36, border 12.87 / 8.80 (12.14 / 8.06 on hover), focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
